Law Commission licence page https://lawcommission.gov.np/en/?p=11910 and FAOLEX https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/nep40222.pdf. Madi Municipality survey: https://nepjol.info/index.php/nvj/article/view/55855 (70% of 122 shops registered, 1.6% of butchers aware of the rules, 11.5% used disinfection).
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Nepali: मासु पसल बधशाला सफ्टवेयर): no Nepal meat-shop or abattoir compliance product found; only generic Nepali custom developers (WebSNP) and foreign butcher POS (Gofrugal, India).
candidates.name: Meat shop and slaughterhouse licence and inspection pack
candidates.trigger: Animal Slaughterhouse and Meat Inspection Act 1999 (2055 BS) and Regulation 2001 (first amendment 2081): licence for slaughterhouses and meat shops, pre-slaughter health check, post-slaughter inspection and certificate before sale. Phased enforcement: Nov 17 2026 (Kathmandu, Lalitpur, Bhaktapur), Jan 15 2027 (other metropolitan, sub-metropolitan and municipal areas), Jul 17 2027 (rural municipalities). Amendment to raise fines proposed. Food Hygiene and Quality Control Act 2081 also applies (exact name unverified).
candidates.unchecked: Whether inspection is digital (no portal mentioned); inspector capacity; who holds the licence register (palika vs DLS); fee levels; real count of meat shops; butchers' willingness to pay is likely low and offline-first; whether the Nov 2026 start actually happened.

candidates.unchecked: Renewal cycle and fees; whether shops must keep batch or prescription registers; DDA notice contents; any online council system; one-off registration drive rather than recurring duty.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Domestic workers were brought under Labour Act and Social Security Act in 2017; municipalities struggle to register them; only ~1,500 informal/self-employed workers in SSF vs ~2.7m total (ILO campaign). No household-employer filing duty or tool found. Weak candidate C08.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No national licensing regime found; only local-government scrap collection fee/contract (old Supreme Court case from Pokhara). Municipal business registration only. Nothing usable.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Nepal-specific rule on second-hand dealers or pawnbrokers found; search returned other countries. Whether the AML Act covers them is unconfirmed (unverified).

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05 (not re-searched, per contract).

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No federal scrappage policy or dismantler licence in Nepal. Public vehicles over 20 years are not renewed; provincial rules differ (Madhesh 2023: 20/25/30 years). No dismantler register to build on.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Only quarantine and import rules found (private quarantine sites need a DLS recommendation; imports through quarantine check posts). No haat-bazaar or animal-transport permit regime or online system found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Mandatory meat inspection phases in under the Animal Slaughterhouse and Meat Inspection Act (licence for slaughterhouses and meat shops, ante- and post-mortem inspection, meat inspector certificate): Nov 17 2026 in Kathmandu Valley, Jan 15 2027 in other urban local bodies, Jul 17 2027 in rural municipalities. Amendment with higher fines proposed. New candidate C01.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Budget: no search spent; no evidence either way.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Animal Health and Livestock Service Practitioners Council (Act certified Asoj 2079, council formed Kartik 2080) requires registration of all animal-health and livestock-service practitioners, classes A-D, fine up to Rs 50,000 and/or 6 months; 10,653 permitted by Oct 2024. Supreme Court directed amending the Medicines Act 2035 to give vets prescribing rights. DDA has a notice on record-keeping of production/import (unread). Candidate C02.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Boring permits sit with KUKL (Kathmandu), District Water Offices and local government; enforcement against unpermitted bores is weak and responsibility overlaps (2025 study). No periodic filing duty found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: WASH Regulation promulgated 23 Jan 2025; Ministry of Water Supply began piloting with 12 service providers on 7 Mar 2025, including faecal sludge treatment plants and water users committees. Haulers' permits are not documented. Candidate C05.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Labour Act 2074 s.78 says inspection of pressure plants and boilers is as prescribed; no lift/boiler inspection regime, notice or register found. Not a viable lead on current evidence.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Same WASH Regulation 2025 pilot as category 11 (service providers and Water and Sanitation Users Committees in Kakarvitta, Waling, Birendranagar). Candidate C05.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Pesticide Act 2019 (2076 BS) and Pesticide Regulation 1993; Plant Quarantine and Pesticide Management Centre registers, licenses import/manufacture/trade/commercial use and keeps an import and sales database. Retailer licence terms and renewal not found. Candidate C03.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Covered by K02. New evidence: ekantipur 27 Jun 2026 reports manpower renewals will be withheld for agencies not resolving complaints, effective Shrawan 1; the minimum-100-workers renewal rule is contested.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Only a law-firm explainer on funeral service licences surfaced (nitipartners.com), unread. No search spent.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: NGOs and associations renew with the Social Welfare Council (progress report, audited accounts, tax clearance, AGM minutes; sources conflict on annual vs three-yearly) and with the DAO/ward/tax offices. Parliamentary committee asked SWC to cancel non-renewing NGOs. Guthi and user-group rules not found. Candidate C04.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Euro 5/6 import standards 2025; Kathmandu emission testing resumed Dec 2025 with fines Rs 5,000 up to Rs 100,000; Pokhara e-ticketing law; DoTM GPS/CCTV/digital ticketing proposal (status unclear); online driver licence from Shrawan 1 2083. No operator-side filing duty identified. Candidate C07 (weak).

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers are covered by K06. Street vendor and market trader rules not searched (budget).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools need DoTM approval and many lack it or have not renewed; draft transport law would require school training certificates for licence applicants. Child development centres follow local government standards. No Nepal tattoo rules found. Hunting outfitters not applicable. Small food producers not searched. Candidate C06.

candidates.unchecked: Whether individual social-media sellers (not platforms) must register; documents needed; whether the duty recurs (renewal, disclosure updates); whether the free state portal is easy enough to make a paid helper pointless; willingness to pay of micro-sellers; sources disagree on the Act year and fine size.

coverage.category: 36. (Nepal) Land and property registration under the Land Revenue Regulations (8th amendment 2082)
coverage.found: Covered by the real estate licence lead. The AML directive 2082 required bank statements and KYC, then the first amendment removed them within about a week (June 2025), so the rules keep changing.
